tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: Find contacts by text (name, email, title), status, source, company or a custom field. Returns up to `limit` contacts and a next_cursor. Requires the read_crm scope.

tools.name: upsert_contact
tools.description: Create a contact, or update the one that already has this email (matched case-insensitively). Custom `fields` and `tags` are merged into what is stored. A company is created or reused from company_domain or company_name. Requires the write_crm scope.

tools.name: update_contact
tools.description: Change fields of an existing contact, found by id or email. Custom `fields` are merged with the existing ones. Requires the write_crm scope.

tools.name: create_deal
tools.description: Open a deal, optionally linked to a contact (by id or email) and a company. Stages: lead, contacted, qualified, proposal, won, lost. The deal takes its contact's company unless company_id is given. Unknown arguments are rejected with unknown_field. Requires the write_crm scope.

tools.name: move_deal
tools.description: Set a deal's stage (lead, contacted, qualified, proposal, won, lost). Requires the write_crm scope.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Attach a note to a contact (by id or email) or to a deal. Requires the write_crm scope.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Create a follow-up task or reminder with an optional due date, on a contact or a deal. Requires the manage_tasks scope.

tools.name: list_due_tasks
tools.description: What is due now: overdue and due-today tasks first, then the next 7 days. Tasks on contacts who replied, unsubscribed or bounced are flagged follow_up_blocked: do not chase those. Requires manage_tasks or read_crm.

tools.name: draft_email
tools.description: Draft one email to a contact. Drafts are auto-approved by default (the operator can switch approval on for the workspace or for you; then the draft waits in their Approvals inbox). Approved mail that cannot be sent to the recipient yet waits in the operator's To send list and the response says so. R

tools.name: list_email_status
tools.description: Status of this agent's emails: pending_approval (only when approval is on), approved (with a note when it waits in the manual To send hand-off), rejected (with reject_reason to learn from), sent, failed, cancelled. Each email carries warnings (open_draft_exists, emailed_N_days_ago) and prior_emails.

tools.name: list_replies
tools.description: Replies captured from contacts, newest first. Requires the read_crm scope.

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: Sent mail and replies for one contact in time order. Requires the read_crm scope.

tools.name: mark_replied
tools.description: Record that a contact replied (optionally with the reply text). Sets the contact to replied, cancels their pending drafts and open follow-up tasks, and stops further drafts to them. Requires the write_crm scope.

tools.name: get_policy
tools.description: What the operator allows this agent: the workspace approval setting and, in plain words, what happens to your CRM writes and email drafts (apply or auto-approve at once, or wait for approval), this agent's mode (direct or propose), daily send caps and how many were used today, blocked domains, and t

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.description: Create a campaign: an ordered sequence of email, wait and task steps run per contact, with follow-ups, stop rules (reply, bounce, unsubscribe and deal stage change stop a contact's sequence), a send window, caps and A/B variants. Pass steps inline, and optionally `enroll` to select contacts in the s

tools.name: update_campaign
tools.description: Change a campaign's settings and/or replace its ordered steps. Editing the steps of a running campaign needs the operator's approval when approval is on. Requires the manage_campaigns scope.

tools.name: get_campaign
tools.description: One campaign with its steps, status, delivery mode (dry run or live) and counters.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: Campaigns in this workspace with status, delivery mode and enrolled/sent/replied counters. Archived ones are hidden unless status=archived.

tools.name: enroll_contacts
tools.description: Enroll contacts by ids, tag, source/list, status, text or custom fields. Suppressed, replied, unsubscribed, bounced, address-less and blocked-domain contacts are skipped with a reason, and a contact in another running campaign is skipped (or moved with on_conflict=move). dry_run=true returns who wou

tools.name: simulate_campaign
tools.description: What would go out over the next N days: per contact and step, the send time (UTC and local), the fully rendered subject and body, and the status (will_send, skipped_missing_variable, skipped_condition, blocked_by_cap, task_created), plus problems and launch_blockers. Nothing is written or sent. It u

tools.name: launch_campaign
tools.description: Start a draft campaign. Refused with launch_blockers (postal address, sender name, an email step, enrolled contacts, a verified identity) until they are fixed. With approval on, it returns 202 and waits for the operator to approve the launch once. Requires the manage_campaigns scope.

tools.name: pause_campaign
tools.description: Freeze a running campaign. Nothing is lost: resuming shifts every pending step by the length of the pause. Requires the manage_campaigns scope.

tools.name: resume_campaign
tools.description: Resume a paused campaign. Requires the manage_campaigns scope.

tools.name: stop_enrollment
tools.description: Stop a single enrollment (reason manual). Requires the manage_campaigns scope.

tools.name: campaign_report
tools.description: Counts per campaign, per step and per variant: enrolled, active, completed, stopped (by reason), sent, sent_dry (dry-run records, nothing delivered), skipped (by reason), replied, bounced, unsubscribed, meetings, deals_created. Rates say which count they divide by.

tools.name: get_outbox
tools.description: For a campaign that sends through your own sender (relay identity): the operator-approved messages you may send now, each with its exact text, recipient, step and evidence link, plus batch_id and batch_hash. Send the text byte for byte, then call report_send for every message. 409 batch_not_approved

tools.name: report_send
tools.description: Report one outbox message: sent (final: the person moves to the next step; reporting sent twice is fine, a different second report is 409 already_reported), refused_cap, refused_unsigned or failed_transient (the message stays in To send and gives its cap unit back), refused_suppressed (the person is

tools.name: list_sending_identities
tools.description: The identities a campaign can send through: the built-in dry_run identity and any the operator connected (their keys are never shown), with their delivery state.

tools.name: add_suppression
tools.description: Never email this address or domain again, in any campaign. Open enrollments of matching contacts stop. Removing an entry needs the operator. Requires the manage_campaigns scope.

tools.name: list_suppressions
tools.description: Addresses and domains that are never emailed.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "draft_email" is 967 chars, far longer than this server's median (184). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_contacts, create_deal, draft_email, list_email_status, get_thread, get_policy, get_outbox, add_suppression · Private data: search_contacts, upsert_contact, update_contact, create_deal, add_note, create_task, list_due_tasks, draft_email, list_replies, get_thread, mark_replied, get_policy, create_campaign, enroll_contacts, simulate_campaign, launch_campaign, campaign_report, add_suppression · Public sink: search_contacts, upsert_contact, update_contact, create_deal, add_note, draft_email, list_email_status, get_policy, create_campaign, simulate_campaign, launch_campaign, get_outbox, report_send, list_sending_identities, add_suppression · Destructive: create_campaign, get_campaign, campaign_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_contacts, create_deal, draft_email, list_email_status, get_thread, get_policy, get_outbox, add_suppression · Private data: search_contacts, upsert_contact, update_contact, create_deal, add_note, create_task, list_due_tasks, draft_email, list_replies, get_thread, mark_replied, get_policy, create_campaign, enroll_contacts, simulate_campaign, launch_campaign, campaign_report, add_suppression · Public sink: search_contacts, upsert_contact, update_contact, create_deal, add_note, draft_email, list_email_status, get_policy, create_campaign, simulate_campaign, launch_campaign, get_outbox, report_send, list_sending_identities, add_suppression · Destructive: create_campaign, get_campaign, campaign_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
